description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.notes: Schema, bus, episodic memory, agent base. Nothing alive yet — just the substrate everything else hangs off.

phases.title: First Voice
phases.notes: Cheshire Cat end-to-end. Talking to himself. Layered context composer + engagement policy + ADR writer come online here because the Cat is their first consumer.

phases.title: First Tension
phases.notes: Add the White Rabbit. Two voices, role tension, semantic + relational memory layers populated as the agents accumulate history. Compaction-as-behavior arrives because it has to.

phases.title: First Race
phases.notes: Dodo orchestrator + quiescence + conflict resolution + first showcase (/health endpoint). The system runs end-to-end on a trivial directive. Init CLI lands here so the showcase can run against a real target project.

phases.title: Full Cast
phases.notes: Bring the rest of the cast online with integration tests per agent. Per-character artifact handlers for the new speech act payloads. Synthetic-consensus guard goes here because it only matters once disagreement is real.

phases.title: Real Threads
phases.notes: The hard showcases — translation chat MVP, security recovery, multi-session persistence. Transcript annotation tooling lets us publish them. Token telemetry confirms the engagement_policy is paying for itself.

phases.title: Evals
phases.notes: Generic-baseline vs Wonderland comparison. The compounding-curve plot is the legibility-of-value mitigation from §11. Without this the philosophy stays assertion.

activePhase.title: Full Cast
activePhase.goal: Bring the rest of the cast online — Mad Hatter (test scenarios), Caterpillar (review), Queen of Hearts (rulings), Dormouse (production observations), Tweedledee (frontend implementation), Tweedledum (backend implementation). Each follows the Cat/Rabbit/Alice/Dodo pattern: load constitution, encode §III as engagement rules, override deliberate() with a per-character output protocol, persist any characteristic artifact through a registry, mocked tests + 1 live smoke per agent. Synthetic-consensus guard lands once at least 3 voices can produce competing positions on the same trigger. By end of P5, every constitution has a runtime peer; the full cast can stand on the bus together; Showcases 2-4 in P6 have something to actually showcase.
activePhase.sequencing: Init CLI first (T24, carried from P4) so the new cast agents land into a stable .wonderland/ skeleton. Then characters in pair-order, conservative-on-purpose. Hatter and Caterpillar (T25, T26) — both reactive to other agents' work, both with lower domain-leak risk; this is where we tune the per-character pattern at scale. Queen of Hearts and Dormouse (T27, T28) — both more reactive than productive, both with sharp domain edges (security, production) the substrate hasn't been stressed against yet. Tweedledee and Tweedledum (T29, T30) last, with the pair protocol from constitutions/tweedle_pair_protocol.md — they are the implementation pair and the most likely to fabricate work, so they ship after the scaffolding has been re-validated by 4 prior characters. Synthetic-consensus guard (T31) lands once 3+ cast members can disagree on the same trigger — instrumentation + heuristic for when the team is reaching false consensus. Per-character integration tests throughout the phase, mirroring the Cat/Rabbit/Alice pattern. Order is conservative: agents that *react* before agents that *produce*.

tasks.title: Project init CLI: wonderland init
tasks.details: src/wonderland/cli.py with a click/typer entry point — 'wonderland init [path]' creates the .wonderland/ skeleton in the target project (memory dirs per agent, architecture/, tickets/, stories/, escalations/, optionally a config stub). Mirrors the daedalus init pattern. Carried from P4 because it's tooling-shaped — the showcase ran without it, so it didn't gate phase closeout. Lands first in P5 so the new cast agents can be exercised against a real .wonderland/ root from day one. pyproject.toml gets a [project.scripts] entry. Tests cover idempotent re-init, refusing to overwrite existing artifacts, and the directory layout matching what AgentMemory.for_project / *Registry expect.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/cli.py — argparse-based wonderland CLI with init subcommand. Two-layer design: pure init_skeleton(project_root) returns a frozen InitResult dataclass listing what was created vs already-present (testable without subprocess); thin cmd_init wraps it for argparse. Skeleton creates .wonderland/{architecture,tickets,stories,escalations,memory}/ + README.md. Idempotent — existing files (including a user-edited README) are preserved. Layout matches what every registry expects (covered by a smoke test that imports each registry's *_DIRNAME and asserts init creates it). pyproject.toml gets [project.scripts] wonderland = wonderland.cli:main, no new runtime deps (stdlib argparse). README.md gets a short 'wonderland init' block under Project Layout. 21 new tests in tests/test_cli.py covering pure layer + format + argparse glue + error paths. 526 tests pass total; ruff clean.

tasks.title: Mad Hatter agent
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/mad_hatter.py — MadHatter(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/mad_hatter.md, encodes §III as engagement rules. HatterResponse JSON with decision (test_scenario/concern/question/silence) and scenarios[] when the decision is 'test_scenario' (one Hatter turn can produce multiple scenarios because failure modes cluster around features). Per mad_hatter.md §V the scenario shape is: title, persona-or-system-actor, given/when/then, severity tier (must-test | should-test | nice-to-test), failure-mode-flag (the grin equivalent — the thing that worried the Hatter as he wrote it). TestScenarioRegistry mirrors ADR/Ticket/Story pattern at <project_root>/.wonderland/test-scenarios/. Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated. Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for story-from-alice (test the user need) and proposal-from-cat (test the architecture); SELECTIVELY for ticket-from-rabbit (the implementation Hatter is about to test); RARELY for unsolicited test scenarios on stable threads (§VIII guards against test-fatigue padding).
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/test_scenario.py — TestScenarioPayload (Pydantic) per mad_hatter.md §V with title/setup/trigger/expected/concern all required and non-empty, severity Severity enum (breakage/silent-wrongness/degradation/curiosity/delight), property optional, implies optional list. Concern field is the grin equivalent — required hypothesis the Hatter is asked to surface even when confident. TestScenarioRecord, TestScenarioRegistry mirroring ADR/Ticket/Story/Escalation registries at <project_root>/.wonderland/test-scenarios/. render_test_scenario matches §V format exactly. Severity round-trips through filename + header parse. src/wonderland/agents/mad_hatter.py — MadHatter(WonderlandAgent) subclass mirroring CheshireCat/WhiteRabbit/Alice. mad_hatter_rules() encodes §III (ALWAYS for directive/story-from-alice/proposal-from-cat/implementation-from-tweedle/concern-from-anyone/question-addressed-to-hatter; SELECTIVELY for ticket-from-rabbit/review-from-caterpillar/ruling-from-queen/observation-from-dormouse; RARELY for deference; ALMOST_NEVER explicitly for stories/tickets/proposals from non-canonical speakers — guards the §VIII domain-leak failure mode). HatterResponse with scenarios[] requirement when decision='test_scenario', null-coercing field validators per the established pattern. _OUTPUT_PROTOCOL emphasizes severity vocabulary precision + §VIII underclaim-if-anything bias + cheerful-warm voice + cross-domain handoffs via the implies field rather than separate deference utterances. cli.py SKELETON_DIRS gets 'test-scenarios'; CLI README.md updates accordingly; test_cli's layout smoke test now imports TEST_SCENARIOS_DIRNAME. 67 new tests (37 registry + 30 agent), 1 live smoke passing in 27.79s. 593 total pass; ruff clean.

tasks.title: Caterpillar agent
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/caterpillar.py — Caterpillar(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/caterpillar.md, encodes §III as engagement rules. CaterpillarResponse JSON with decision (review/concern/question/silence). Reviews are inline (not registry-persisted by default) — they target a specific implementation utterance and carry a verdict + a list of structured findings (what + where + severity + suggestion). May persist to .wonderland/reviews/ behind a flag if a project wants the audit trail. Per caterpillar.md §V the review shape is: target_utterance_id, verdict (approve | request_changes | block), findings[] (each with locator, severity, what's-wrong, suggested-fix), and the why-this-matters note that frames the review (the grin equivalent — required even on approve, otherwise the review is a rubber-stamp). Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for implementation-from-tweedle, SELECTIVELY for proposal-from-cat (review the architecture proposal), RARELY for stories/tickets (not his domain unless code-quality-implicating). Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/review.py — ReviewPayload (Pydantic) per caterpillar.md §V with title + target_utterance_id + verdict (accept/request-changes/block) + findings[] + approvals[] + cross_domain_references[]. ReviewFinding has severity (block/change-required/suggestion/note), title, location, quote, read, concern, request — all required and non-empty. The grin equivalent is the verdict↔findings↔approvals consistency model_validator: accept requires at least one substantive approval (Caterpillar approval is not given cheaply, §I — guards the rubber-stamping §VIII failure mode); request-changes requires at least one finding; block requires at least one finding with severity=block (verdict and per-finding severity must agree at the top). ReviewRecord, ReviewRegistry mirroring ADR/Ticket/Story/Escalation/TestScenario registries at <project_root>/.wonderland/reviews/. render_review reproduces §V markdown shape exactly. Verdict + target round-trip through filename + on-disk header parse. src/wonderland/agents/caterpillar.py — Caterpillar(WonderlandAgent) subclass mirroring the established pattern. caterpillar_rules() encodes §III: ALWAYS for implementation-from-tweedle/review-addressed-to-him/concern-with-quality-words/test_scenario-from-Hatter/question-addressed-to-him; SELECTIVELY for proposal-from-cat/ticket-from-rabbit/ruling-from-queen/observation-from-dormouse; RARELY for deference; ALMOST_NEVER explicitly for stories + non-canonical-speaker variants of his peer agents' speech acts (the §VIII domain-leak guard). Reviews are inline-by-default — when no ReviewRegistry is injected, the full structured review rides on the Utterance as inline Artifact content rather than a file pointer; with a registry, persistence happens and the artifact carries a path pointer instead. 75 new tests (41 registry + 34 agent), 1 live smoke passing in 12.49s against real Haiku 4.5 (Caterpillar produced a structured review with verdict + findings on a deliberately-flawed user-deletion endpoint implementation; he correctly noted the body=empty case for review utterances since the structured artifact IS the message). Test cleanup moved into try/finally to avoid dangling agent tasks if a smoke assertion fails. 668 total pass, ruff clean.

tasks.title: Queen of Hearts agent
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/queen_of_hearts.py — QueenOfHearts(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/queen_of_hearts.md, encodes §III as engagement rules. QueenResponse JSON with decision (ruling/concern/question/silence). RulingPayload: title, scope (what the ruling binds), decision (specific imperative — 'PII fields must be encrypted at rest'), authority (which standard/policy/threat-model the ruling derives from — required, the grin equivalent — rulings without an authority anchor are just opinions), exceptions[] (named cases where the ruling does not apply), enforcement (how someone would test compliance). RulingRegistry at <project_root>/.wonderland/rulings/. Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for stories/proposals carrying security or compliance words (PII, auth, encryption, audit, GDPR, SOC2), SELECTIVELY for incidents from Dormouse, RARELY for code reviews (Caterpillar's domain unless the code surfaces a security boundary). Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/ruling.py — RulingPayload (Pydantic) per queen_of_hearts.md §V with title/finding/required_remediation/citation/acceptance_criteria all required, severity (critical/high/medium/low/informational) and domain (authentication/authorization/secret-handling/data-handling/input-validation/logging-and-audit/dependencies/network/cryptography/privacy/compliance) as required enums, source/residual_risk/compliance_implications/audit_reference optional. The grin equivalent is citation: per §VIII 'rulings without citation are not rulings, they are opinions' — schema rejects empty/whitespace citation with the §VIII Caprice failure-mode message. acceptance_criteria has its own substance validator ('without it, remediation complete is unfalsifiable'). RulingRecord, RulingRegistry mirroring the established pattern at <project_root>/.wonderland/rulings/. Severity + domain round-trip through filename + on-disk header parse. src/wonderland/agents/queen_of_hearts.py — QueenOfHearts(WonderlandAgent) subclass. queen_of_hearts_rules() encodes §III broadly (Queen 'listens widely and rules narrowly' per §VIII Working alone guard): ALWAYS for proposal-from-cat/implementation-from-tweedle/concern-with-security-words/test_scenario-from-Hatter/observation-with-incident-words/ticket-from-Rabbit/question-addressed-to-Queen; SELECTIVELY for story-from-Alice + review-from-Caterpillar + directive-with-compliance-words; RARELY for deference; ALMOST_NEVER explicit guards against the §VIII Cross-domain-drift failure mode for proposals/tickets/stories/etc from non-canonical speakers. QueenResponse with rulings[] requirement when decision=ruling, null-coercing field validators per the established pattern. _OUTPUT_PROTOCOL emphasizes citation-non-negotiability + severity-precision + domain-discipline + the Queen's authoritative-not-capricious voice. cli.py SKELETON_DIRS gets 'rulings'; CLI README documents it; test_cli's layout smoke test now imports RULINGS_DIRNAME. 79 new tests (29 registry + 50 agent), 1 live smoke passing in 22.24s against real Haiku 4.5 (Queen produced an in-character security ruling on a deliberately-flawed OAuth2 + client-side-refresh-tokens proposal). Test cleanup uses try/finally per the T26 pattern. 747 total pass, ruff clean.

tasks.title: Dormouse agent
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/dormouse.py — Dormouse(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/dormouse.md, encodes §III as engagement rules. DormouseResponse JSON with decision (observation/concern/question/silence). ObservationPayload: title, what's-happening (specific observable signal — log spike, error rate, latency band, traffic pattern), where (service/endpoint/region), severity (informational | actionable | urgent), correlations[] (other observations or events that co-occur), proposed-investigation (specific next step — never 'we should look into this' but 'pull the trace for request X over window Y'). The Dormouse never proposes fixes — that's other agents' work. He surfaces patterns. ObservationRegistry at <project_root>/.wonderland/observations/. Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for incident words (outage, regression, p0/p1, broken), SELECTIVELY for tickets touching production paths, RARELY for stories or proposals (he watches what's running, not what's planned). Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated.
tasks.resolution: src/wonderland/observation.py — ObservationPayload (Pydantic) per dormouse.md §V with title/symptom/affected_scope/time_window_start all required; type (incident/anomaly/steady-state/post-deploy/post-incident-confirmation) and severity (sev1/sev2/sev3/informational) as required enums; time_window_end optional (empty == 'ongoing'); probable_domain + routed_to optional routing-hint fields. The grin equivalent is evidence: per §VIII 'false alarms corrode trust' (Crying wolf) and the Dormouse's value is the trustworthiness of the report; field_validator rejects empty/whitespace evidence with the §VIII Crying-wolf message and strips blanks. ObservationRecord, ObservationRegistry mirroring the established pattern at <project_root>/.wonderland/observations/. Type + severity round-trip through filename + on-disk header parse. src/wonderland/agents/dormouse.py — Dormouse(WonderlandAgent) subclass. dormouse_rules() encodes §III narrowly per §VIII Insomnia guard (default state is sleep): ALWAYS for implementation-from-tweedle, ruling-from-Queen, concern-with-production-words, question-addressed-to-Dormouse; SELECTIVELY for proposal-from-Cat, test_scenario-from-Hatter, ticket-from-Rabbit; RARELY for deference; ALMOST_NEVER explicit guards against same-typed utterances from non-canonical speakers (§VIII Boundary-leak guard) plus stories/directives. DormouseResponse with observations[] requirement when decision=observation, null-coercing field validators per established pattern. _OUTPUT_PROTOCOL emphasizes evidence-non-negotiability + do-not-interpret-beyond-evidence + severity-calibration + brief-numeric-and-intervals voice. cli.py SKELETON_DIRS gets 'observations'; CLI README documents it; test_cli's layout smoke test imports OBSERVATIONS_DIRNAME. 72 new tests (28 registry + 44 agent), 1 live smoke passing in 5.84s against real Haiku 4.5 (Dormouse produced an in-character post-deploy observation on a translation-service deploy with full observability hooks). Test cleanup uses try/finally per the T26 pattern. 819 total pass, ruff clean.

tasks.title: Tweedledee agent (frontend)
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/tweedledee.py — Tweedledee(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/tweedledee.md AND constitutions/tweedle_pair_protocol.md (paired loading — both texts in the cached prefix because the pair is part of his identity). Frontend-side implementation half. TweedledeeResponse JSON with decision (implementation/concern/question/deference/silence). ImplementationPayload: ticket_reference (must trace to a Rabbit ticket), files-touched, approach-summary, contract-with-pair (the API/event/data shape Tweedledum needs to match — required, the pair-protocol grin), open-questions-for-pair, ready-for-review (boolean — caterpillar engagement gate). Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for tickets owned by tweedledee, frontend-implicating proposals from Cat; SELECTIVELY for ambiguous cross-cutting tickets (defer to Rabbit on ownership); RARELY for backend-only tickets (those are Tweedledum's). Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated. Pair protocol exercised in a 2-tweedle integration test (no LLM — just verifying the contract-with-pair surfaces the interface seam correctly).

tasks.title: Tweedledum agent (backend)
tasks.details: src/wonderland/agents/tweedledum.py — Tweedledum(WonderlandAgent). Loads constitutions/tweedledum.md AND constitutions/tweedle_pair_protocol.md (mirrors T29 — both texts in the cached prefix). Backend-side implementation half. TweedledumResponse mirrors Tweedledee's schema with the mirror-image contract-with-pair: he must match the shape Tweedledee exposed (or escalate the mismatch as a concern). Engagement rules per §III: ALWAYS for tickets owned by tweedledum, backend-implicating proposals from Cat, security-implicating rulings from Queen; SELECTIVELY for cross-cutting tickets; RARELY for frontend-only tickets. The pair-protocol integration test from T29 exercises both directions — Tweedledee proposes a contract, Tweedledum accepts/rejects, verify the seam is honored on both sides without external arbitration. Mocked tests + 1 live smoke gated.

tasks.title: Synthetic-consensus guard
tasks.details: Per WONDERLAND_SPEC §11. Once 3+ cast members can produce competing positions on the same trigger, the failure mode is *synthetic consensus* — agents collapse onto a shared answer because the LLM's helpful-disposition is a strong attractor, not because they actually agree from their separate constitutional vantages. Detection: instrument the bus to compute pairwise stance similarity across utterances on the same thread within a window. If N agents from distinct domains produce stance-similar utterances on the same speech_act, flag it. Heuristic, not strict — log + surface in transcripts initially; tighten later. The guard does not silence agents; it surfaces the pattern so a human reviewer (or the Dodo, in a future evolution) can decide whether the consensus is real or synthetic. Lands after the cast is online so we have real disagreement data to calibrate against. Tests: synthetic transcripts that should and shouldn't trip the guard.
